history.dynasty: Bushahr (royal family of the erstwhile Bushahr state)
history.period: Medieval to modern (complex ~13th century / ~800 years old; new temple 1943)
history.summary: The Narsingh shrine is one of the subsidiary shrines inside the Bhimakali Temple complex at Sarahan, not a standalone temple. The Bhimakali complex — dedicated to Goddess Bhimakali, kuldevi of the former Bushahr rulers and revered as one of the 51 Shakti Peethas — is about 800 years old (traditionally dated to the 13th century) and built in Kath-khuni (alternating stone and timber) hill architecture. The sacred compound holds both the old and new Bhimakali temples plus separate shrines to Narsingh, Raghunath and Patal Bhairava (Lanka Bir); the Narsingh shrine stands in shikhara style in the first courtyard behind the gold-plated first gate. The old temple was damaged by the 1905 Kangra earthquake and a new temple was completed in 1943; Raja Padam Singh contributed to rebuilding in the 1920s and silver doors were commissioned by Raja Shamsher Singh in the 19th century. The Narsingh shrine shares the complex's worship and visitor arrangements; no separate founding date or dedicated shrine history is documented in the sources consulted (UNVERIFIED as a distinct institution).

name: Narsingh Shrine, Bhimakali Temple complex
town_description: Sarahan is a small town in the Rampur region of Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, sitting at about 2,300-2,400 metres in the Sutlej valley. It was the former summer capital of the Bushahr kingdom and is dominated by the famous Bhimakali Temple complex. The town is a gateway viewpoint for the snow-covered Shrikhand Mahadev peak and draws pilgrims and tourists from across the state.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism — Narasimha avatar of Vishnu, within a Shakta temple complex)

travel.airport: Jubbarhatti Airport (Shimla) — approximately 155-160 km (verify); Sarahan is ~180 km from Shimla by road on NH-5
travel.railway: Shimla Railway Station — approximately 165-175 km (verify); Kalka is the broad-gauge railhead beyond Shimla
travel.road: On NH-5 (Shimla-Rampur road), about 180 km from Shimla via Rampur; taxis and HRTC buses available from Shimla and Rampur

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November for clear weather; Dussehra and Navratri are the major festival seasons
visitor_information.opening_hours: Complex open roughly sunrise to sunset (verify). Daily aartis: Mangala Arati ~6:00 AM in summer (~7:30 AM in winter), ~8:00/9:00 AM arati, noon bhog arati, and evening Sandhya Arati after sunset (verify)
